wrong_version.answer:
Connection timeout (Ironclad v2) > Where the setting lives
The timeout is `connection_timeout_seconds` in `ironclad.conf`, in the `[source]` block. It takes a whole number of seconds. The default is **30 seconds**.

```
[source]
connection_timeout_seconds = 30
```

Connection timeout (Ironclad v2) > Where the setting lives
The timeout is `connection_timeout_seconds` in `ironclad.conf`, in the `[source]` block. It takes a whole number of seconds. The default is **30 seconds**.

```
[source]
connection_timeout_seconds = 30
```

Connection timeout (Ironclad v2) > Limits
The lowest accepted value is 5. The highest accepted value is 300. A value outside that range is rejected at startup and the runner refuses to start, with `E1104: connection_timeout_seconds out of range` in the startup log.

Connection timeout (Ironclad v3) > Where the setting lives
The timeout is the environment variable `IRONCLAD_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, in whole seconds. The default is **15 seconds**.

```
export IRONCLAD_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=15
```

`connection_timeout_seconds` in `ironclad.conf` is no longer used. If it is sti

Authentication (Ironclad v2)
Every call to the Ironclad API must identify the caller.

Authentication (Ironclad v3) > Failures
The `X-Ironclad-Key` header is no longer accepted. A request carrying it is rejected with `401` and the body `{"error":"scheme_removed"}`, which is the error to look for after an upgrade. A missing or expired token returns `401` with `{"error":"bad_token"}`.

Authentication (Ironclad v2) > Failures
A missing or unknown key returns `401` with the body `{"error":"bad_key"}`.

Export format (Ironclad v2)
An export writes the result of a run to a file.

Export format (Ironclad v3) > Encoding
UTF-8 **without a byte-order mark**. Spreadsheet software that relied on the mark to detect the encoding may now show accented characters incorrectly on first open.

Export format (Ironclad v2) > Quoting
A field is quoted only when it contains a comma, a quotation mark or a newline.

Log retention (Ironclad v2) > How long logs are kept
`log_retention_days` in `ironclad.conf` sets the number of days. The default is **14 days**. Logs older than that are deleted by a sweep that runs at startup and then once a day.

```
[runner]
log_retention_days = 14
```

Log retention (Ironclad v3) > How long logs are kept
`IRONCLAD_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` sets the number of days kept on disk. The default is **7 days**. Logs older than that are deleted by a sweep that runs at startup and then once an hour.

```
export IRONCLAD_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS=7
```

Log retention (Ironclad v2) > How long logs are kept
`log_retention_days` in `ironclad.conf` sets the number of days. The default is **14 days**. Logs older than that are deleted by a sweep that runs at startup and then once a day.

```
[runner]
log_retention_days = 14
```

Retries (Ironclad v2) > Settings
`retry_count` in `ironclad.conf` sets how many retries follow the first attempt. The default is **3**. The interval between retries is fixed at **5 seconds** and cannot be configured.

```
[source]
retry_count = 3
```

Retries (Ironclad v3) > Giving up
After the last retry the run is marked `failed` and the partial output is **kept** under `runs/<run-id>/partial/`, so a long transfer can be resumed with `ironcladctl resume <run-id>`.

Retries (Ironclad v2) > What is retried
Every failure is retried, including a rejected credential and a malformed request. A run that fails for a reason retrying cannot fix therefore takes `retry_count * 5` seconds longer than it needs to.

Scheduling runs (Ironclad v2) > How schedules are written
Schedules live in `schedules.conf`, one per line, as a five-field cron expression followed by the pipeline name.

```
0 2 * * *  nightly-export
*/15 * * * *  inbox-poll
```

All times are interpreted in **UTC**. There is no timezone setting;

Scheduling runs (Ironclad v3) > Overlap
If a scheduled run is still going when the next one is due, the next one is **queued** and starts when the first finishes. At most one run is queued; further ones are dropped with a warning.

Scheduling runs (Ironclad v2) > Catching up
Runs missed while the runner was stopped are not started when it comes back.

Connection timeout (Ironclad v3) > Limits
The lowest accepted value is 1. The highest accepted value is 120. A value outside that range is rejected at startup and the runner refuses to start, with `E1104: IRONCLAD_CONNECT_TIMEOUT out of range` in the startup log.

Connection timeout (Ironclad v2) > Where the setting lives
The timeout is `connection_timeout_seconds` in `ironclad.conf`, in the `[source]` block. It takes a whole number of seconds. The default is **30 seconds**.

```
[source]
connection_timeout_seconds = 30
```

Authentication (Ironclad v3)
Every call to the Ironclad API must identify the caller.

Authentication (Ironclad v3) > How to authenticate
Exchange your client credentials for a bearer token, then send the token in the `Authorization` header on every request.

```
curl -X POST https://api.example-ironclad.test/v3/oauth/token \
  -d grant_type=client_credentials -d client_id=... -d clie

Authentication (Ironclad v2) > How to authenticate
Send your API key in the `X-Ironclad-Key` header on every request.

```
curl -H 'X-Ironclad-Key: <your key>' https://api.example-ironclad.test/v2/runs
```

Keys are created in the console under Settings, Access. A key **does not expire** and remains

Authentication (Ironclad v3) > Failures
The `X-Ironclad-Key` header is no longer accepted. A request carrying it is rejected with `401` and the body `{"error":"scheme_removed"}`, which is the error to look for after an upgrade. A missing or expired token returns `401` with `{"error":"bad_token"}`.

Export format (Ironclad v3) > Formats
CSV or NDJSON, chosen with `IRONCLAD_EXPORT_FORMAT`, which defaults to `csv`. The CSV separator is a comma and cannot be changed.

Export format (Ironclad v2) > Encoding
UTF-8 **with a byte-order mark**, so that the file opens correctly in spreadsheet software without extra steps.

Export format (Ironclad v3) > Formats
CSV or NDJSON, chosen with `IRONCLAD_EXPORT_FORMAT`, which defaults to `csv`. The CSV separator is a comma and cannot be changed.

Log retention (Ironclad v3) > How long logs are kept
`IRONCLAD_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` sets the number of days kept on disk. The default is **7 days**. Logs older than that are deleted by a sweep that runs at startup and then once an hour.

```
export IRONCLAD_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS=7
```

Log retention (Ironclad v2) > How long logs are kept
`log_retention_days` in `ironclad.conf` sets the number of days. The default is **14 days**. Logs older than that are deleted by a sweep that runs at startup and then once a day.

```
[runner]
log_retention_days = 14
```

Log retention (Ironclad v3) > Where logs are written
`/var/log/ironclad/<run-id>.log` as before, and each closed log is also uploaded to the export bucket under `logs/<date>/<run-id>.log.gz`, where it is kept for **365 days** regardless of the on-disk setting.

Retries (Ironclad v3) > Settings
`IRONCLAD_RETRY_MAX` sets how many retries follow the first attempt. The default is **6**. `IRONCLAD_RETRY_POLICY` takes `exponential` or `fixed` and defaults to `exponential`, starting at **2 seconds** and doubling, capped at 60 seconds.

```
export IRONCLAD_RETRY_M

Retries (Ironclad v2) > Settings
`retry_count` in `ironclad.conf` sets how many retries follow the first attempt. The default is **3**. The interval between retries is fixed at **5 seconds** and cannot be configured.

```
[source]
retry_count = 3
```

Retries (Ironclad v3) > What is retried
Only failures that retrying can fix: timeouts, connection resets, and responses with status 429 or 5xx. A rejected credential or a malformed request fails the run immediately, without retrying.

Scheduling runs (Ironclad v3) > How schedules are written
Schedules are set per pipeline in the console, or through `IRONCLAD_SCHEDULE`, as an ISO-8601 repeating interval with an explicit timezone.

```
export IRONCLAD_SCHEDULE='R/2026-01-01T02:00:00[Europe/London]/P1D'
```

Cron expressions are **n

Scheduling runs (Ironclad v2) > Overlap
If a scheduled run is still going when the next one is due, the next one is **skipped** and a warning is written to the log.

Scheduling runs (Ironclad v3) > Catching up
Runs missed while the runner was stopped are started once when it comes back, unless `IRONCLAD_SCHEDULE_CATCHUP=false`.

`IRONCLAD_RETRY_MAX` sets how many retries follow the first attempt. The default is **6**. `IRONCLAD_RETRY_POLICY` takes `exponential` or `fixed` and defaults to `exponential`, starting at **2 seconds** and doubling, capped at 60 seconds.

```
export IRONCLAD_RETRY_M

Retries (Ironclad v2) > Settings
`retry_count` in `ironclad.conf` sets how many retries follow the first attempt. The default is **3**. The interval between retries is fixed at **5 seconds** and cannot be configured.

```
[source]
retry_count = 3
```

Retries (Ironclad v3) > What is retried
Only failures that retrying can fix: timeouts, connection resets, and responses with status 429 or 5xx. A rejected credential or a malformed request fails the run immediately, without retrying.

Scheduling runs (Ironclad v3) > How schedules are written
Schedules are set per pipeline in the console, or through `IRONCLAD_SCHEDULE`, as an ISO-8601 repeating interval with an explicit timezone.

```
export IRONCLAD_SCHEDULE='R/2026-01-01T02:00:00[Europe/London]/P1D'
```

Scheduling runs (Ironclad v2) > Overlap
If a scheduled run is still going when the next one is due, the next one is **skipped** and a warning is written to the log.

Scheduling runs (Ironclad v3) > Catching up
Runs missed while the runner was stopped are started once when it comes back, unless `IRONCLAD_SCHEDULE_CATCHUP=false`.
